stem: A team is sketching a job graph and wants each step to be a first-class task rather than code hidden inside a notebook. One proposed step is a direct call to an external HTTP service, and the team must confirm whether the job UI offers that as its own task type.

option_texts.A: A REST API call step is offered, and calling a remote endpoint is a supported task type
option_texts.B: A Python wheel step is offered, and running a wheel is a supported task type
option_texts.C: An If/else condition step is offered, and branching is a supported task type
option_texts.D: A SQL step is offered, and running a statement is a supported task type

drill_answer_short: Notebook, Python wheel, SQL, Pipeline, dbt, JAR, If/else and For each are task types; a REST API call is not
decision_hinge: The task types available include Notebook, Python script, Python wheel, SQL, Pipeline, Ingestion pipeline, Dashboards, dbt, JAR, Spark Submit, Run Job, If/else, and For each.

plausible_options.C: wants each step to be a first-class task rather than code hidden inside a notebook

eliminated_by.B: One proposed step is a direct call to an external HTTP service
eliminated_by.D: the team must confirm whether the job UI offers that as its own task type

distractor_traps.B: T2: scope error - a Python wheel is a genuine task type, so it is not the odd one out
distractor_traps.C: T3: confusable sibling - If/else is a real control-flow task type and belongs to the list
distractor_traps.D: T2: scope error - SQL is a genuine task type and does appear in the job UI

stem: One task in a production job has to stop running for a fortnight while an upstream system is rebuilt. The team wants the task left out of the next runs, but wants its configuration and its past run history preserved so it can come back untouched.

option_texts.A: Delete the task and rebuild its configuration from a neighbouring task later on
option_texts.B: Disable the task, which skips it at run time while it keeps its configuration
option_texts.C: Set the task dependency to a condition that can never be met in the next runs
option_texts.D: Pause the whole job schedule, then start each run by hand without that task

drill_answer_short: Disabling a task skips it at run time without removing it; configuration and run history survive
decision_hinge: Disable a task to skip it at run time without removing it from the job; the task keeps its configuration and run history, so you can re-enable it later without rebuilding the task.

plausible_options.C: wants the task left out of the next runs

eliminated_by.A: wants its configuration and its past run history preserved
eliminated_by.D: One task in a production job has to stop running for a fortnight

distractor_traps.A: T4: breaks a stated requirement - deleting the task discards exactly what has to be preserved
distractor_traps.C: T3: confusable sibling - an unmeetable condition also skips the task, but it edits the graph the team wants untouched
distractor_traps.D: T2: scope error - pausing the schedule stops every task, not the single one named

stem: A new joiner asks how the platform can offer ACID guarantees over plain files in cloud object storage. The team must describe what the storage layer actually adds on top of the underlying columnar files.

option_texts.A: It copies every file into a relational database that provides the ACID guarantees
option_texts.B: It replaces Parquet with a proprietary binary container that records each transaction
option_texts.C: It extends Parquet data files with a file-based transaction log for ACID transactions
option_texts.D: It locks the storage account for the duration of each write so writers cannot overlap

drill_answer_short: Delta Lake extends Parquet data files with a file-based transaction log that provides ACID transactions
decision_hinge: Delta Lake is open source software that extends Parquet data files with a file-based transaction log for ACID transactions.

plausible_options.B: what the storage layer actually adds on top of the underlying columnar files

eliminated_by.A: how the platform can offer ACID guarantees over plain files in cloud object storage
eliminated_by.D: The team must describe what the storage layer actually adds

distractor_traps.A: T1: fabricated - no copy into a relational engine takes place
distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling - the format stays open Parquet, with a log beside it rather than a proprietary container
distractor_traps.D: T5: common misconception - concurrency comes from the transaction log, not from locking the account

stem: An engineer runs CREATE TABLE without naming any format, then wonders which on-disk layout the resulting table uses. Nothing in the workspace configuration has been changed from its delivered state.

option_texts.A: Parquet, because the platform writes plain columnar files until a format is named
option_texts.B: CSV, because an unqualified table falls back to a text layout that any tool can read
option_texts.C: JSON, because the metadata layer stores unqualified tables in a document layout
option_texts.D: Delta, because it is the default format for all operations on the platform

drill_answer_short: Delta Lake is the default format for all operations on Databricks
decision_hinge: Delta Lake is the default format for all operations on Databricks.

plausible_options.A: wonders which on-disk layout the resulting table uses

eliminated_by.B: runs CREATE TABLE without naming any format
eliminated_by.C: Nothing in the workspace configuration has been changed from its delivered state

distractor_traps.A: T3: confusable sibling - Parquet is the underlying file format, but the table default is Delta
distractor_traps.B: T1: fabricated - no unqualified table falls back to a text layout
distractor_traps.C: T1: fabricated - table data is never stored in a document layout by default

stem: A retailer's batch pipeline is light for most of the month and very heavy during seasonal peaks. It currently runs on compute with a fixed number of workers sized for the peak, and the finance team has challenged the bill for the quiet weeks.

option_texts.A: Enable autoscaling with a minimum and maximum, so workers follow the shape of the job
option_texts.B: Keep the fixed size but shorten the schedule so the compute is up for fewer hours
option_texts.C: Size the fixed compute with fewer workers for the quiet weeks and accept slower peaks
option_texts.D: Split the pipeline across two fixed compute resources so each one is smaller

drill_answer_short: Autoscaling moves workers between a minimum and maximum, cutting cost against a statically sized resource
decision_hinge: With autoscaling Databricks dynamically reallocates workers to account for the characteristics of your job, and autoscaling can reduce overall costs compared to a statically-sized compute resource.

plausible_options.B: the finance team has challenged the bill for the quiet weeks

eliminated_by.D: runs on compute with a fixed number of workers sized for the peak

distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling - fewer hours does trim cost, but the resource is still over-provisioned while it runs
distractor_traps.C: T4: breaks a stated requirement - the peak work still has to finish on time
distractor_traps.D: T5: common misconception - two fixed resources are still fixed and still mis-sized

stem: A query writes FROM students JOIN enrolments ON students.id = enrolments.student_id with no further keyword before the word JOIN. A reviewer asks which rows the statement will return.

option_texts.A: Every row from the left reference, because an unqualified join keeps the left side whole
option_texts.B: Only rows with matching values in both references, because that join-type is the default
option_texts.C: Every row from both references, because an unqualified join forms the full product
option_texts.D: Only rows from the left reference with no match, because the default suppresses matches

drill_answer_short: INNER is the default join-type, returning rows that have matching values in both table references
decision_hinge: INNER returns the rows that have matching values in both table references, and it is the default join-type.

plausible_options.A: no further keyword before the word JOIN

eliminated_by.C: A reviewer asks which rows the statement will return

distractor_traps.A: T3: confusable sibling - that is LEFT OUTER behaviour, which has to be asked for by name
distractor_traps.C: T5: common misconception - a cross product needs CROSS JOIN and ignores the ON clause
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated - suppressing matched rows is LEFT ANTI, never the default

stem: A silver job has to list the customers that appear in the orders table but are missing from the approved customers table. The output must carry columns from the orders side only, with no duplicate rows introduced by the comparison.

option_texts.A: A LEFT SEMI join, which returns the left rows that do have a match on the right
option_texts.B: A LEFT OUTER join, which returns all left rows and pads the unmatched ones with nulls
option_texts.C: A LEFT ANTI join, which returns the left rows that have no match on the right
option_texts.D: A CROSS join filtered afterwards, which compares every pair and keeps the misses

drill_answer_short: LEFT ANTI returns rows from the left reference that have no match in the right one
decision_hinge: A LEFT ANTI join returns the values from the left table reference that have no match in the right table reference, and a LEFT SEMI join returns the ones that do match.

plausible_options.B: list the customers that appear in the orders table but are missing from the approved customers table

eliminated_by.A: The output must carry columns from the orders side only
eliminated_by.D: with no duplicate rows introduced by the comparison

distractor_traps.A: T3: confusable sibling - LEFT SEMI is the exact complement and returns the matched rows
distractor_traps.B: T2: scope error - an outer join returns the matched rows too, padded rather than filtered out
distractor_traps.D: T5: common misconception - a cross product multiplies rows before any filter runs

stem: A team new to the platform is choosing the service that will coordinate a nightly chain of notebooks, a SQL statement and a pipeline, with dependencies between them. They want one scheduled workflow rather than three things triggering each other.

option_texts.A: An external scheduler that drives the workflow by hitting the workspace API per step
option_texts.B: A single notebook that calls the other notebooks in sequence through dbutils
option_texts.C: A SQL warehouse query schedule, which runs each statement at a chosen time
option_texts.D: Lakeflow Jobs, which schedules and orchestrates tasks as part of a larger workflow

drill_answer_short: A job schedules and orchestrates tasks in a workflow, each task being a unit of work with dependencies
decision_hinge: In Databricks a job is used to schedule and orchestrate tasks in a workflow, providing orchestration for data processing workloads so that you can coordinate and run multiple tasks as part of a larger workflow.

plausible_options.A: They want one scheduled workflow rather than three things triggering each other

eliminated_by.B: a nightly chain of notebooks, a SQL statement and a pipeline

distractor_traps.A: T3: confusable sibling - an external scheduler can drive the API, but the platform ships the orchestrator
distractor_traps.B: T2: scope error - a driver notebook hides the dependencies and gives no per-step observability
distractor_traps.C: T2: scope error - a query schedule runs statements and cannot orchestrate a pipeline task
